### 2026-10-26: ## W4: Holographic Clock Display

**3h**

## W4: Holographic Clock Display
### The prototype

I went with a much simpler (hopefully!) design this week because of exams!

This session was spent building prototypes for my holographic display.

Pepper's Ghost visual effects are created by securing a thin piece of transparent material at a 45° angle on top of a screen. This allows a viewer to see what is displayed on the screen without seeing the surface itself.

There are two ways I could have implemented this in my design, and I wanted to sus out each option:

* Using an inverted square pyramid, with a seperate image on each face. This creates a 3D-effect
* Using a single tilted piece of glass. This better utilises the whole surface of the underlying display

### The inverted square pyramid prototype

I started by scoring a large piece of acrylic into small, triangle shaped pieces (this took wayyyy too long!!!):

![IMG_8470 Large](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/b28f652b21025924c43b8e6e3ea4196480502fdd1d2eeedf49ae62f7904bb337.jpg)

![IMG_8471 Large](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/63345f23bf464f69c0ccacde8c0fea6806417b2c1f04ec291740a774b6f414dd.jpg)

I then assembled the pyramid:

![IMG_8476 Large](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/96cc72b7bf00b181a9c15765efa8076a4a66e1a8918eebca2e4a446a01a825cc.jpg)

I then used a jellyfish image to test my prototype (sorry about the blurry image).

![IMG_8474 Large](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/e19f8a2de129a312e7097c171cf8408993b8b7ee161b9cd516574eda46cec511.jpg)

The advantage of this is that each edge of the pyramid can have its own image, giving a 3D effect. However, the need for 4 seperate displays, or 1 much larger display, could complicate the PCB design.

### The tilted glass prototype

This prototype was much simpler. After scoring the acrylic sheet into an 8x8cm square, I arrived at the following:

![IMG_8478 Large](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/c0c28bcc51db1125b9041e6edd03484a7b2349a15259ad851adc2d42400b5a32.jpg)

The jellyfish is still visible even as the screen gets much further away, as long as it's directly above:

![IMG_8479 Large](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/30bb674e3e7631087a6f85c5ee1b288af0a48db414e02208c2ca9697f7c1e6bb.jpg)

The advantage of this is it makes PCB and casing design much simpler, while only allowing one viewing angle.

### The verdict

I decided to go with the pyramid, as it will allow me to better create 3D effects and feel more polished as a project.

Next up is selecting parts, then schematic and PCB design, casing, and firmware!

Thanks for reading :)

### 2026-10-29: ## W4: Holographic Display

**6h**

## W4: Holographic Display
### Selecting parts, designing the schematic, and assembling the casing

Going with the pyramid display idea, the key contraint was that I would need 4 small displays that can be powered at the same time by an ESP-32. I searched through components on LCSC, as this would save on shipping since you can purchase it at the same time as JLCPCB and JLC3DP orders.

As well as the displays, I searched for buttons, for effect selection, and a thumbwheel potentiometer for brightness control. I also needed to purchase male headers to secure all the pieces together. For the microcontroller, I decided to use the XIAO ESP-32 due to its small footprint, however as this was not on LCSC the cost of the controller plus the shipping ended up being around ~$10. I arrived at the following:

```
W4:
  SEED Studio
    Microcontroller:
      https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO-RP2040/ (~$10)
      (footprints / schematics: https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/XIAO-RP2040/#resources)

  LCSC:
    Displays:
      4 * https://www.lcsc.com/product-detail/C7471924.html ($8.88)

    Buttons (for image selection):
      https://www.lcsc.com/product-detail/C49393619.html

    Potentiometer (for brightness control):
      https://www.lcsc.com/product-detail/C470643.html

    Male Headers (for connecting everything together):
      https://www.lcsc.com/product-detail/C2337.html

    (these combined are around ~$3)

  JLC:
    PCB: ~$4
    Casing: ~$2

  Plastic / glass pyramid / panel (any reflective plastic you have lying around)

  shipping: ~$5

  total: just under ~$30
```

### The schematic

I first sourced the footprints and symbols of my parts online:

![IMG_8487 Large](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/bc6fa8fabd93013522adc899f28dbb9fac37ceee51ef95062e48aa52599d588f.jpg)

![IMG_8489 Large](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/d88ac59598061be0fcee5577aeed49a9403565cf279c48a0721291b4d9c58a89.jpg)

Note all the display share most SPI data connections, including CLK, SDA, BLK etc. The only difference is each display has its own CS (chip select) line, allowing me to drive all of them at once, or alternatively select each one seperately and display different images in each.

I then assembled the layout of my PCB:

![IMG_8490 Large](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/319fb369885603097653e9f5fb52adb1dbde9405fffae7a8a2653f8586ed9316.jpg)

...and exported the 3D model:

![IMG_8491 Large](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/48d1dcb7e3488913412d36d3d5626032478eabb8976cb368e6a5961d746db690.jpg)

### What's next

Next up is routing the PCB, adding drill holes to secure it to the casing, adding the holder for the reflective material, and finally writing the firmware.

### 2026-10-31: ## W4: Holographic Clock Display

**8h**

## W4: Holographic Clock Display
### Completing the Schematic, PCB & Casing

A lot of work was done this session completing the CAD part of this week's project.

### PCB & Schematic

I first had to finalise the schematic. I found that some wires were incorrectly connected upon testing in the PCB editor, and so I had to fix these. I then finalised the layout of my PCB:

![IMG_8490 Large](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/319fb369885603097653e9f5fb52adb1dbde9405fffae7a8a2653f8586ed9316.jpg)

I then began connecting the ratlines. This took me quite a while, and I found my wiring to be quite messy and complicated, as all 4 screens had to share display & power lines. It looked a bit like this:

![IMG_8508 Large](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/674e6fd5e2377f5d484868dfa627e333676a8106b4b69db3c15e7f81c730a227.jpg)

I then added a copper fill connected to the GND net:

![IMG_8510 Large](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/18ef1c728cd177a0e3ede53a67a123ef4f2b3ff756dadc5233a7cc7621dfcc19.jpg)

The finalised PCB ended up looking like the following:

![IMG_8512 Large](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/6d65cafe509df48822e399616eb8305fd72b855f20acff923fa50f2c162cdf2c.jpg)

After passing DRC, I exported Gerber & Drill files in both compressed and uncompressed format, as well as STEP & STL 3D outputs. These, as well as the KiCad project files, were uploaded to my GitHub repository.

### 3D-Printed Casing

I began by adding a ledge in the casing for the PCB to lean on, holding it at the correct height 4.4mm above the base:

![Screenshot 2026-10-31 at 17.52.20](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/3d7dd42ecdc937ba4f761c33aaf3392dbb229cb352142eced35a90c2d4908e33.png)

I then began work on the roof of the case. The roof as the same size as the base of the case, with a bottom lip the same size as the PCB to prevent the roof from slipping out. A small hole was indented in this lip to make room for the USB-C cable. Using the screen's datasheet, as well as some calculations, I made some holes in the roof for the screens.

![Screenshot 2026-10-31 at 18.36.33](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/feb92c8d216876e148c5c932acc1e1ea3949353e1a83f656eb90a4203f9bd900.png)

I then calculated the height / width of the pillars that will hold the transparent pieces. They will be 3cm in width at the top of the roof, and just under 9cm in width at the top of the structure. In Onshape I did alter my computed values a bit, however, to get the right padding and spacing.

![IMG_8513 Large](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/6cefa3caca34e41bf9d76f2af58a6a5cae954a301c3497a4be36946b54b2e105.jpg)

Rotating the transparent pieces:

![Screenshot 2026-10-31 at 19.03.06](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/c67dd1f9f31cf2ac94485356d3554a1e42a45419c97ea092dee026327f858c72.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-31 at 19.13.15](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/6ebc23572b0a72f8bb010a7c15ce86d5bb0b8879ee985f84e3b131a5975253b5.png)

With these, I built 4 triangular prisms and indented the holes the trapeziums make:

![Screenshot 2026-10-31 at 20.48.36](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/5660a19c942af55d4026fe80d3acd8e5235e29f0d2dc1b061ce65e53ece7595f.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-31 at 21.10.05](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/fc31152331c7fae5e2adbe40a3168ff4abfa1c10cc1cafd7b7bdd4d7e47b01d1.png)

Finally, I added some screwholes to mount my PCB into the casing. Note that the roof doesn't get mounted on, however as the display won't be moved very often this shouldn't be a problem.

![Screenshot 2026-10-31 at 21.51.37](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/55254291120668a19a4c2767b7f9e788532306c71b03777a156bb81d00450923.png)

The final product looked like this:

![Screenshot 2026-10-31 at 21.54.55](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/dff112b91bc91d39fbbea0a8113c6fcaa31095130c4a5142a67f5cc6d27ccb68.png)

Putting the STEP files into JLC3DP, I found that the final cost would be a few more dollars than I originally anticipated, so I updated the BOM accordingly.

![Screenshot 2026-10-31 at 22.12.54](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/7e03f9c87c9681fe75542728cb9b7ac1258cff9ec0ed4117753949bdaf633e40.png)

All that's left to do is write the README, and firmware for the ESP32!

Thanks for reading :)

## W4: Holographic Display
### Wrapping it up

This session was spent writing the shell of the firmware, and finalising the GitHub repository.

I first wrote some code in Python for my microcontroller. As I don't have the ESP32 or the displays yet, I wasn't able to write any I/O code that would actually display any images, however I did write the shell in that it will be much easier for me to start writing code directly for the displays in build week, as the display & update loops, as well as initialisation, is already set up.

In build week, all my time will therefore be spent on creating cool effects for the displays. The code looked a bit like the following:
